text:
viv: Heads up  I want to start a short thread about tightening the onboarding compatibility story. goal: fewer surprises in production when we swap binaries / quant profiles.

noah: +1. Last week we had two rollouts where runtime ABI mismatch surfaced only under specific seq lengths. Painful.

chen: proposal: bring a lightweight compatibility matrix into ingest metadata. matrix rows: (kernel-abi, quant-mode, max-seq-tested, exports-ok). keep it conservative.

viv: example format analyzer would emit (single-line JSON field in metadata): `compat_matrix: ["abi:v2:fp16:512:true", "abi:v2:int8:256:false"]`

teresa: how do we keep the matrix accurate? analyzer should run a tiny ABI smoke that loads binary, runs 8 deterministic prompts, checks outputs against a golden tolerance. cheap but effective.

noah: agree; also need a liberal fallback rule: if runtime reports `abi-mismatch` at deploy, router should fallback to a compatible model variant (next-best quant/abi) rather than erroring hard.

compat-bot: Note: I've added a lint that flags models without compat_matrix at ingest in staging. Use `--skip-compat-lint` for platform-only uploads.

chen: question: do we allow teams to opt-out of strict compatibility? some internal experiments will need to. maybe an `admit: lax` flag, but then label model as experimental in registry.

viv: yes, opt-out allowed but UX must be clear: experimental models can't be auto-dedicated or used for high-SLA customers. also require an explicit acceptance of risk.

noah: runtime side: add a lightweight shim to detect unsupported ops at load-time and emit a structured error with `op, kernel, suggestion`. that helps us route to fallback.

teresa: tests: add a harness that replays the analyzer's deterministic prompts against every new runtime build. CI should fail a runtime release if we regress compatibility for >1% of registered models.

chen: performance tradeoff: analyzer's smoke should be <= 60s. we can reduce checks by sampling kernels for large models. also cache analyzer results keyed by model fingerprint.

viv: policy: when analyzer says `exports-ok=false` for a quant-mode, we mark that quant-mode as blocked from automatic routing. ops can override for debugging.

noah: rollout: (1) analyzer changes + compat_matrix field (1 week spike), (2) runtime shim & structured errors (1 week), (3) router fallback + UI labels (1 week), (4) 14d canary on a subset of orgs.

teresa: follow-ups: I'll draft the analyzer smoke harness and the deterministic prompt set. prefer per-org golden plus a small public set.

compat-bot: Action created: ONB-2147 "compat-matrix analyzer + runtime shim" assigned to @teresa and @chen.

viv: decision summary: add compat_matrix metadata from a fast analyzer, add runtime shim that emits structured compatibility errors, route to fallback model variants instead of hard failing, and allow explicit experimental opt-outs.

noah: thanks. this should cut a lot of noisy production incidents. :white_check_mark:
